s: Content safety layer that reviews, classifies, and filters user-generated content against policy rules and ML classifiers.
w: Receives content (text, images, video) via API or message queue, runs through a pipeline: automated ML classifiers (toxicity detection, hate speech, nudity), regex/blocklist matching for known bad patterns, and human review queues for ambiguous cases. Actions include: approve, reject, quarantine (shadow ban), or escalate to human review. Feedback loops improve classifier accuracy over time.
use: User-generated content platforms: comments, posts, reviews, chat messages
Marketplace listings: product images and descriptions against policy
AI-generated content safety: reviewing LLM outputs before user exposure
Trust & safety compliance for platform regulatory requirements
avoid: Internal content without user-generated risk (unnecessary latency overhead)
Fully automated moderation without human review escalation for edge cases
Content types the ML classifiers cannot handle (specialized domain content)
pits: False positives silencing legitimate content - tune thresholds and provide appeal mechanisms
Adversarial evasion: users adapting content to bypass classifiers - continuous retraining needed
tips: Human-in-the-loop is essential - fully automated moderation at scale always makes mistakes
Moderation latency impacts user experience - design for async review with fast pre-screening
